correctness.rationale: The renewal first-reset decomposition yields the exact MFPT W(1-e^{-u})/(u^2 sum a_j exp(-a_j u)). The logarithmic derivative is h(u)-2+u mu(u). For u=c/a_j, c in {1/2,2}, exponential separation uniformly bounds |mu(u)/a_j-1|<0.01 for every finite N: smaller sites contribute at most 1/999, larger sites at most 2*1000^2*exp(-500), relative to the own-site term exp(-c). Therefore the derivative is strictly negative at all N left endpoints and strictly positive at all N right endpoints. These windows are disjoint, implying N strict minima and N-1 intervening strict maxima by analyticity and compactness. The standalone script independently tests endpoint bounds, root bracketing, and finite-difference identities (1,287 passing assertions), but the infinite-N conclusion relies on the analytic proof.

originality.rationale: The source arXiv:2311.11897 obtains the N-site renewal expression and analyzes two-site metastability, but its examined Sections III–VI do not supply a bound growing linearly with the number of resetting sites or the geometric-hierarchy construction. The 2020 Gaussian-reset experiment finds one metastable well. The 2024 distributed-reset paper analyzes mean and variance and does not provide a many-well theorem. The exact all-N derivative-bracketing argument, not the antecedent transform, is assessed as new. Targeted external and research-record searches did not identify a result implying this claim; residual priority risk remains.

No independent scholarly originality audit has been performed.

value.rationale: The natural extension of two-site distributed-reset search reveals that a single controllable resetting rate can have unboundedly many metastable locally optimal scales when more reset sites are allowed. The explicit N-site construction and separated-rate windows structurally explain hierarchical multi-timescale search: each remote location introduces another locally favorable rate despite the competing sites. This answers a meaningful model-complexity question beyond known two-site metastability. It is not a routine finite numerical experiment or a claim of N equal global optima; both are clearly excluded.
